title: Every modularly extended finite simple matroid has a divisional flag, so an arrangement with that matroid is divisionally free
author: Shuhei Tsujie
source_title: Modular Construction of Free Hyperplane Arrangements
difficulty_reason: The author must show that successive characteristic-polynomial divisibility survives gluing over round modular flats while the contracted matroid remains in the recursively defined class. The proof develops modular-restriction closure and a rank induction that finds suitable atoms outside a minimal join flat, then transfers their divisionality through contraction. This is substantially beyond the standard graphic-arrangement/chordal-graph criterion or a routine modular-lattice calculation.

proof_review.note: The full new divisional-flag construction of Theorem1.8 was read, including modular-restriction closure Lemma3.1, minimal-round-join induction Theorem3.2 and divisional-atom transfer Lemma2.20. Proposition2.19 supplies the contraction/modular-join geometry and characteristic-polynomial formula explicitly; prior Brylawski modularity and factorization statements are credited background. The new proof finds an atom outside the round join flat and keeps the simplified contraction in ME, permitting recursive construction of the full flag. The separate description of ME by supersolvable joins and gain-graph applications are not counted as neighboring claims.

statement_scope: Exactly Theorem1.8 for finite simple matroids in ME, the minimal class containing the empty matroid, closed under adjoining a modular coatom whose restriction is in ME, and under modular joins of ME matroids over a ROUND flat (Definition1.7). A full-rank flat flag has each characteristic polynomial of a successive contraction dividing its predecessor. Consequently an arrangement A with M(A) in ME is divisionally free in the stated sense. No arbitrary modular join lacking the round condition, all free arrangements, or separate gain-graph classification is claimed.
